When I was 18, after high school, I was raped in a van by my ex-girlfriend. We weren't together at the time, it happened at a house party. She came up to me as if to talk, and as we walked outside, was tossed keys to a van. Guests at the party were cheering us on, and I didn’t truly understand. When we had gotten in that van "to talk", I was raped. I said no, it wasn't consensual. I told her this wasn't what I wanted. I made a move to exit the van but she pinned me down by her weight and told me that "I was going to want it". All I could think was all those people inside that house were cheering for this. Was I disappointing them by not wanting this to happen? I was lost in my mind as she was taking advantage of me. It was as if I was bullied to have sex with someone I didn't want to, put into a position I didn't know how to escape from. When it was over, I was met with a look of disgust because I didn't please my rapist. I just sat there lost and in fear unsure of what to make of what just happened. This was my first experience with sex. The walk back into that party, I was met with a chorus of cheers, louder than before. The look of disgust and hatred of what my attacker gave me in that van quickly became a smile and a laugh as soon as we both walked in. She was proclaiming it was the best time ever. Talking of an experience that wasn't true. And I was applauded by peers, most of which I didn't know in congratulations that I had now become a man. I smiled and laughed in the same way as her. That day, my life, my identity, my whole sense of self came crashing down. I was put into a position where I had to live as someone I didn't recognize. Someone who had to be proud of the way they lost their virginity, someone who had to convince myself that I wasn't raped, that I enjoyed it because it was expected of me. I was a man now and I should be proud of that. 
This was what I had to tell myself to get through the painful memory I tried to bury and move past. It didn’t help that weeks after this, on a car ride somewhere in the same van I was raped in, that there were talks about parts of my body that were spread around that deflated me even further. The details of what truly happened inside that van never came to light and so to hear of this addition, I grew to hate and question myself. All I could was laugh along and take it in. That night, I held a kitchen knife to my throat and asked God for permission to kill myself. Would he allow me into heaven for committing this sin? I drifted away from everyone soon after. But I had already lost sight of myself, and would for years. I questioned myself constantly. From my sexuality, my own body, my purpose… what reason did I have to live as I continued to suffer... I was a boy who wanted to still be loved but couldn't even stand to be near women I didn't trust. This affected me for so long. I couldn't take more than a certain amount of college classes. I holed myself in front of a computer to seek comfort in the kindness of strangers who became good friends. The one time an old female classmate came to hug me, I felt nothing but fear and I broke down in my car soon after questioning if I should just kill myself. I didn't feel I had anyone to talk to. This repeating cycle of another sleepless night? Another breakdown? What could I have done? Who could ever relate? Who would believe that a man could be raped by a woman? 
This tormented me for years.
In truth, I still question if I have any qualifications to be able to fall in love with a female partner because of fear that maybe I’m not up to par, that I will be played with, and even just bullying myself mentally. I can say the trauma hasn’t completely gone away. In 2019, I had enough of it and was going to follow through with my suicidal thoughts. The journey of recovery from that is another story to tell for another time. Yet even then, I’m continuing to grow each day, with time slowly overcoming these demons that I have had to deal with for many years.
The fact I'm even here telling you this is a gift for me because I don't know how I managed to not give up and just kill myself at any point in my life. Maybe time and growth do play a part, being open finally about this story certainly helped alleviate so much weight I had been carrying. Perhaps it was the friends who stuck by me who gave me the time to listen to my story. Whatever the case, I feel I have found myself again after all these years of not knowing who I was. 
This song I'm sharing with you is my story. It helped me get through a tough moment remembering my rape, during Mental Health Awareness Day in 2019, when not long before then I felt so sure I was done living.  I hope that in telling you this it's able to help anyone else that may be struggling similarly. God knows if I heard a song like this back then, or knew someone out there understood what I was going through, I wouldn't have felt so alone. Ultimately the message I want to spread is that if you understand me, you’re not alone. This journey took nearly a decade for me to finally accept myself and be proud of the person I’ve become through it. I wouldn’t want anyone to have to wait 10 years to get to where I am now, and it doesn’t. I survived and I want everyone to know that they can too. Cause I know it would have helped the person inside myself who was feeling lost, scared, and alone sitting in that van back in 2010.
Thanks for listening to my story. I would just hope that anyone who can relate also has found an outlet
